pr_title: Use pulsectl library for PulseAudio connection
pr_body:
<!--
  You are amazing! Thanks for contributing to our project!

## Breaking change
<!--
  If your PR contains a breaking change for existing users, it is important
  to tell them what breaks, how to make it work again and why we did this.
  This piece of text is published with the release notes, so it helps if you
  write it towards our users, not us.
  Note: Remove this section if this PR is NOT a breaking change.
-->

- The default connection honors the configuration in /etc/pulse and no longer defaults to `localhost`
- When a host is configured, the default port has been changed to 4713 to use the native interface of PulseAudio. 
- The config parameters `buffer_size` and `tcp_timeout` have been removed.

## Proposed change
<!-- 
  Describe the big picture of your changes here to communicate to the
  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

Get rid of internal library code and use pulsectl library to communicate
with PulseAudio server.

This is a breaking change as the library uses the much more powerful
native interface instead of the CLI interface, requiring the need to
change the default port.

On the bright side, this also solves some issues with the existing
implementation:

  - There was no test if the complete list of loaded modules was
    already received. If not all data could be read at once, the
    remaining modules not yet in the buffer were considered absent,
    resulting in unreliable behavior when a lot of modules were loaded
    on the server.

  - A switch could be turned on before the list of loaded modules was
    loaded, leading to a loopback module being loaded even though this
    module was already active (#32016).

issue_context.title: pulseaudio: Multiple loopbacks for same switch
issue_context.body:

-->
## The problem

A `pulseaudio_loopback` switch loads another `module-loopback` even though the module for this combination of sink and source is already loaded, resulting in weird audio output as the source is now sent to the sink multiple times.

This seems to be reproducable when restarting Home Assistant when the module is already loaded and a script turns on the switch during startup, see logs below.


<!-- 
  Describe the issue you are experiencing here to communicate to the
  maintainers. Tell us what you were trying to do and what happened instead.
-->


## Environment
<!--
  Provide details about the versions you are using, which helps us to reproduce
  and find the issue quicker. Version information is found in the
  Home Assistant frontend: Developer tools -> Info.
-->

- Home Assistant release with the issue: 0.105.5
- Last working Home Assistant release (if known): 
- Operating environment (Hass.io/Docker/Windows/etc.): Hass.io on Ubuntu
- Integration causing this issue: pulseaudio_loopback
- Link to integration documentation on our website: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/pulseaudio_loopback/

## Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml`
<!--
  An example configuration that caused the problem for you. Fill this out even
  if it seems unimportant to you. Please be sure to remove personal information
  like passwords, private URLs and other credentials.
-->

```yaml
switch:
  - platform: pulseaudio_loopback
    name: audio_kueche_alexa
    source_name: alexa_haus
    sink_name: kueche
```

## Traceback/Error logs
<!--
  If you come across any trace or error logs, please provide them.
-->

Looks like the module is loaded before the state is fetched from the server....

## Additional information
comments: I'm not yet sure what triggers this, but this behavior is not limited to starting up Home Assistant. I also get multiple modules loaded during normal operation. I'm turning audio zones on/off based on presence, but it looks as if turning a switch on when it's already on can also lead to this behavior...

review_comments: Why you need now that settings? He read the local settings from /etc/pulse and do the right thing. However, we can have such settings optional
You're right. I updated the code to default to using the configuration in /etc/pulse....
